title: The event pipeline: stages and execution context

sentences.text: Maya, a sales rep at Contoso, saves a new account in her model-driven app.
The app does not write to the database by itself.
It sends a message called Create to Dataverse.
Dataverse then runs that message through a pipeline of four stages, and your plug-ins join the stages around the save.
Think of a restaurant: the order is checked, prepared, cooked, and finally plated.
The first stop is PreValidation, stage ten.
It usually runs outside the database transaction, and before the security checks.
Contoso registers a synchronous plug-in here.
It sees that the tax number is empty, and throws an Invalid Plugin Execution Exception with a clear message.
Maya reads the message, and nothing was written.
This is the cheapest place to cancel an operation.
Next comes PreOperation, stage twenty.
Now the database transaction is open, but the row is not saved yet.
Contoso's second plug-in tidies the account name before it is written.
Because the plug-in changes the values first, there is no extra update.
Avoid cancelling here.
A cancel triggers a rollback of the whole transaction, and that costs a lot of performance.
Stage thirty is the main operation.
This is where Dataverse itself writes the new account row.
The stage is for internal use, with one exception: the plug-ins of custom A P Is, and custom virtual table data providers, run here.
Everything before it is called Pre, and everything after it is called Post.
The words simply mean before or after this write.
PostOperation, stage forty, runs after the write and still inside the transaction.
Contoso creates a follow-up task for Maya here, with a synchronous plug-in.
If that plug-in throws an error, the whole transaction rolls back, and the new account disappears too.
Also avoid changing the same account here, because that triggers a brand new Update event.
Not every job must make Maya wait.
In PostOperation you can register an asynchronous step.
It goes into a queue and runs after the operation completes, outside the database transaction.
It never joins that transaction, so if it fails, the account stays saved.
Only PostOperation allows asynchronous steps.
Contoso uses one to send the welcome email.
On the exam, remember four rules.
To cancel an operation, use a synchronous PreValidation step and throw an Invalid Plugin Execution Exception.
To change values before they are saved, use PreOperation.
Asynchronous steps exist only in PostOperation.
And an exception in any synchronous stage rolls back the whole transaction.
Never build logic on the Depth property.
